findings.evidence: Naming conventions: "_-separated strings in a lemma name correspond to a definition name or connective". Mathlib's `ρ`-suffixed names (`Rep.trivial_ρ`, `Rep.tensor_ρ`, `FDRep.hom_hom_action_ρ`) all refer to the `ρ` projection.
findings.fix: Rename to `isSemisimple_representation_apply` (the name the PR description itself uses) or follow the adjacent general-representation lemma `TauCeti.Representation.isSemisimple_of_pow_eq_one` (Values.lean:111) and use `isSemisimple_apply`; update the module docstring at line 50.
findings.issue: `isSemisimple_ρ` names the bound variable `ρ : Representation (ZMod p) G V`, not a declaration in the conclusion. The repo precedent `TauCeti.FDRep.isSemisimple_ρ` (TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/CharacterTable/Values.lean:226) is legitimate because `ρ` there is the projection `FDRep.ρ` occurring in `V.ρ g`; here no declaration named `ρ` appears, so no `_`-separated component corresponds to a definition.

findings.evidence: Naming conventions: the name describes the conclusion; both explicit arguments of `IsGoodDixonPrime G p` are part of it. The existing names also collide conceptually with any future second certificate for the same group.
findings.fix: Include the prime, e.g. `isGoodDixonPrime_dihedralGroup_four_five` and `isGoodDixonPrime_dihedralGroup_three_seven` (or `..._five_dihedralGroup_four`), consistent with Mathlib's `Nat.prime_two`/`Nat.prime_three` naming a specific numeral.
findings.issue: `isGoodDixonPrime_dihedralGroup_four : IsGoodDixonPrime (DihedralGroup 4) 5` omits the second argument of the predicate; the name reads as "`DihedralGroup 4` has a good Dixon prime" (the weaker existence claim) rather than "5 is one". Same at line 83, `isGoodDixonPrime_dihedralGroup_three : IsGoodDixonPrime (DihedralGroup 3) 7`.

summary: Names are largely Mathlib-conformant and the roadmap-prescribed names are used correctly; two naming defects: a lemma named after a bound variable, and the two dihedral certificates omitting the prime they certify.
